attributes.summary: Initial T1 authored: divergent-sources-of-truth problem statement, git-as-source-of-truth premise, methodology overview, draft event ontology (26 events in 5+1 categories, 7 entity types), sequential per-commit extraction approach, three-tier storage (events.jsonl + SQLite + snapshots), pre-commit hook lifecycle, plugin structure outline.

attributes.title: Hand-rollable end-to-end
attributes.summary: First milestone. Capability unlock: end-to-end tracker pipeline working against this project, hand-rolled. Touches T2-ontology, T2-storage, T2-projection, T2-packaging. ~10 T3 tasks. Explicitly excludes automated extraction (M2), cleanliness gate (M3), install on fresh project (M4), backfill (M5), and snapshots.

attributes.title: Formal event + entity ontology
attributes.summary: T2 plan for the ontology theme. Captures event types, entity types, derived states, and attribute schemas as both prose (in T1 §4) and machine-readable JSON Schema artefacts. M1-scheduled T3s: events.schema.json, plan-frontmatter.schema.json. Validation runs at cache build (M1), extraction (M2), and merge gate (M3).

attributes.title: Event log, cache, projection storage
attributes.summary: T2 plan for the storage theme. The data layer — events.jsonl (canonical), SQLite cache (queryable), projection.json (view-friendly), snapshots (later). M1-scheduled T3s: cache-sqlite-schema, projection-json-shape, git-blame-commit-ref.

attributes.title: Views and queries over the event log
attributes.summary: T2 plan for the projection theme. Derived views — markdown summaries, HTML visualisations, query patterns — over the event log via SQLite cache and projection.json. M1-scheduled T3s: projection-emitter, markdown-summary, html-view-template, projection-queries-v0.

attributes.title: Plugin scaffold and distribution
attributes.summary: T2 plan for the packaging theme. Plugin directory structure + build/test loop in M1; distribution mechanic (npm bundle, install command, Cowork verification) in M4. M1-scheduled T3s: plugin-scaffold, build-loop.

attributes.title: Create plugin directory structure
attributes.summary: First M1 T3. Creates the plugin scaffold at repo root (agent-plan-tracker/) with full subdirectory layout per T1 §4.11, a minimal Claude Code plugin manifest (format investigated in Step 1), and placeholder files. Acceptance: plugin loads in Claude Code without errors. Unblocks all subsequent M1 T3s by giving them a defined landing location.

attributes.title: Per-commit extraction + merge lifecycle
attributes.summary: New T2 absorbing T1 §4.1 (sequential per-commit extraction) and §4.8 (extraction and merge lifecycle). M2 territory primarily — per-commit extraction agent, pre-commit hook, sub-agent recursion, ambiguity halting; M3-scheduled cleanliness gate and merge conflict handling. Reuses extractor primitive in T2-ingest.

attributes.title: Backfill + retrospective mapping
attributes.summary: New T2 covering one-shot backfill of existing project histories + the retrospective mapping note for non-native projects. M5 territory. Reuses T2-extraction's per-commit extractor primitive. Includes mapping-note format and generation, backfill orchestration, resumability.

attributes.title: HTML view visual style decisions needed
attributes.summary: Concrete style choices for the HTML view: colour palette per derived state, typography, card layout, tree-visualisation choice (D3 / SVG / CSS), responsive considerations, decision-arc click affordance. Resurrect when M1 functional view ships.

attributes.title: Snapshot auto-trigger configuration
attributes.summary: Configure snapshot auto-roll cadence (N events) per project, plus manual-trigger slash command, plus major-plan-closure auto-trigger. Resurrect when snapshots become useful (M2/M3).

attributes.title: Verification overhaul — probably-closed/actually-closed split
attributes.summary: Replace 4-event verification category (claimed/tested/skipped/failed) with 2-event split (probably-closed + actually-closed with schema-enforced different-actor requirement). Trust-by-second-opinion built into the ontology. Resurrect after M1 dogfooding produces ~10-20 plan completions via current model.

attributes.title: Side quest formalisation — when to spawn a lettered workstream
attributes.summary: Initial intuition: spawn when (a) work doesn't fit any single T2's scope AND (b) work has its own coherent why-how-what worth a T1-equivalent. Otherwise extend an existing T2. To be refined through dogfooding; likely becomes a philosophy doc.

attributes.title: Final plugin name decision
attributes.summary: Working name agent-plan-tracker. Alternatives: plan-spine, git-plan, apgt, aplan, apath. apt rejected. Decide before M4 publish.

attributes.title: M2 extraction prompt template — initial structure
attributes.summary: Initial skeleton for the per-commit extractor prompt: role+purpose, ontology summary, input contract, output contract, examples per event type, ambiguity-halt protocol, methodology grounding, token-cost discipline. Per empirical-prompt-architecture, start static; iterate from failures. Resurrect when T3-events-schema-json lands.

attributes.title: Retrospective mapping note generator agent (M5)
attributes.summary: Agent that surveys a non-native repo's planning artefacts and proposes a draft mapping note for human review. Cautious by default; confidence-tagged mappings; proposes-doesn't-commit. Lives in agent-plan-tracker/agents/. Integrates with backfill flow as a pre-flight step.

attributes.title: Initial content for cheatsheet.md
attributes.summary: Common operations table mapping want-to verbs to scripts/<name> invocations. Pair with one-liner explanations; cross-link worked-examples. Resurrect when first M1 tooling lands (probably T3-projection-queries-v0).

attributes.title: Cowork vs Code — altitude-specific guidance
attributes.summary: Guidance on when to use Cowork (T1/T2 planning altitude) vs Code (T3 execution altitude). Possibly plugin UX hints; possibly a philosophy doc; possibly a skill. Speculative; resurrect when Cowork is used in earnest on this project.

attributes.title: Meta — autopilot invoked for documentation persistence (not its intended use)
attributes.summary: This session used oh-my-claudecode:autopilot for documentation persistence rather than code generation. The boulder-never-stops principle scoped the work usefully; phases didn't fully map. Suggests candidate skills: /persist (snapshot conversation to disk), /migrate-plans (restructure plans safely), /dogfood-pass (flag methodology drift). Resurrect when designing similar non-code persistence skills.

attributes.title: Methodology rule: agents must emit entity.created for plans
attributes.summary: When emitting events for a plan that doesn't already exist in events.jsonl, agents must include an entity.created event with the plan's frontmatter as attributes — even for one-event lifecycles. The cache builder materialises entities.attributes only from entity.created; without it, downstream projections lose plan_kind/tier/t2_parent/milestone and entities get mis-routed (e.g. fell through to 'Other' swimlane in the flow view). Workaround: cache-build now reads frontmatter as fallback.

attributes.title: On-demand 'what is outstanding?' analysis via Claude — server endpoint
attributes.summary: Click LIVE badge currently shows entity timeline (cache-derived) but not 'what specifically is outstanding'. Proposed: ~80-line Python wrapper around http.server that adds /api/analyse?entity_id=X endpoint, builds context (plan md + timeline + related), invokes claude CLI, returns analysis. Defer until project has >5 live entities at once or running against external M5 projects.

attributes.title: T2-analyser — On-demand 'what's outstanding?' analysis over live entities
attributes.summary: Browser-direct Anthropic API call + thin server wrapper. New event types analysis.live-summary and analysis.invalidated. Per-summary markdown files in .agent-plan-tracker/summaries/. Clean-tree guard before save. Summary chain (each new supersedes previous) avoids retreading. Cascade invalidation when underlying state shifts. Bulk mode with prompt caching for 'analyse all live'. 5 phases A-E (~7-8h total) candidate-scheduled across later milestones.

attributes.title: M1.1-analyser — On-demand 'what's outstanding?' analyser, rolled out across five phases
attributes.summary: Renamed M6-analyser -> M1.1-analyser via the event-sourced identity-migration primitive. The analyser was always conceptually the FIRST sub-milestone of M1 (M1 extension/hardening, surfaced during M1) but was historically mislabelled M6 and, during M1.2, grandfathered under that flat label + reparented to M1-bootstrap rather than renumbered. This rename reverses that grandfather decision now that entity.renamed is built: cache-build folds the rename (old id->new id) across the entity's own ~8-event history, its 6 child edges, and frozen frontmatter seeds, leaving zero phantom M6 rows and no resurrection (derived_state stays closed; entity.renamed is state-neutral). First milestone on the dotted Mn.p sub-milestone scheme.

attributes.title: T3-analyser-phase-a-ephemeral — Browser-only analyser proof of value (no persistence)
attributes.summary: Phase A of M6: ship a working 'Analyse outstanding' button on the flow view's LIVE-badge sidebar. Click → cost dialog → confirm → Claude API call (browser-direct with anthropic-dangerous-direct-browser-access) → structured + freeform summary rendered. No save, no events.jsonl write, no server wrapper. Exercises §3.12 programmatic context building for the first time. 7 implementation steps; ephemeral by design — close tab = summary gone. Acceptance: real Anthropic call returns useful structured summary in <15s; no regression on existing views.

attributes.title: T3-analyser-phase-b-persistence — Persistence, new event types, server wrapper, opportunistic derived
attributes.summary: Phase B of M6: turn ephemeral analyser summaries into persisted events. Ontology grows: analysis.live-summary (saved structured + freeform pointer; source primary|derived; supersession chain) and analysis.invalidated (Phase D will fill cascade logic; Phase B stubs the endpoint). Schema bumps to 0.2.0 with loosened schema_version enum so old 0.1.0 events stay valid. Server wrapper at agent-plan-tracker/scripts/serve.py replaces python3 -m http.server: subclasses SimpleHTTPRequestHandler, binds 127.0.0.1, exposes /api/clean-check, /api/save-summary, /api/invalidate-summary (501 stub). Per-summary markdown files at .agent-plan-tracker/summaries/<entity_id>-<event_id>.md. Clean-tree guard via git status --porcelain refuses save on dirty tree. Browser-side: Save button on result panel; SavedSummary view becomes the default sidebar render when a saved summary exists for the entity; Regenerate button rebuilds. Opportunistic derived caching: system prompt asks Claude to emit summaries for 1-hop dependents; server enforces primary-beats-derived supersession. cache-build extends with new summaries table; projection emits latest_summary_by_entity. repack-validate passes end-to-end.

attributes.title: T3-analyser-phase-c-flow-rendering — Saved summaries appear as distinct nodes in the workstreams flow
attributes.summary: Phase C of M6: render each analysis.live-summary event as a distinct node on its entity's lifeline in the workstreams flow. Primary summaries = filled purple square; derived = outlined purple square; invalidated = dimmed + strike-through (Phase D will produce actual invalidations; Phase C renders correctly when they exist). Click → opens that specific summary in the sidebar via a new SavedSummary.renderByEventId helper (not always the latest). Pure additive change to computeFlowLayout + renderFlowSVG + style.css. No schema, server, or cache changes.

T3 authored for flow-view density work. Three tasks bundled: (A) sticky + resizable entity-name gutter via sticky HTML overlay over flow-svg-wrap; (B) compact vertical commit labels with hover-tooltip + click-to-detail, shrinking COMMIT_WIDTH 150→44; (C) spawn-relationship navigation in sidebar (parents/children clickable rows) added to showDetail, showLiveStatus, and SavedSummary. Bonus: pink-created colour tweak #c2185b → #e91e63 to disambiguate from fulcrum reds. Out of scope per T2-projection §5 deferrals: filter/search, snapshot selector, vertical sticky for swimlane labels.

attributes.title: T3-analyser-phase-d-cascade-invalidation — Saved summaries invalidatable with cascade detection
attributes.summary: Phase D of M6: operator can invalidate a saved summary; server computes cascade set (same-entity chain successors + 1-hop spawn neighbours after target + derived-summary children whose origin_summary_event_id matches target); emits analysis.invalidated event listing the cascade. Browser surface: Invalidate button on SavedSummary panel + confirmation dialog with cascade preview + reason picker. Invalidated summaries excluded from latest_summary_by_entity chain lookup (Phase B's filter); dimmed/struck through in flow view (Phase C's render path).

attributes.title: T3-analyser-phase-e-global-mode — 'Analyse all live' with Anthropic prompt caching
attributes.summary: Phase E (final phase of M6): 'Analyse all live (global)' toolbar button runs a single sweep over every live entity, sending shared context (T1 + recent events + live-entities index) once with cache_control:ephemeral and reusing it on per-entity follow-on calls. Derived emission suppressed (every entity gets a primary). Progress modal with per-entity status + running cost + cache-hit ratio. Clean-tree re-check between saves. Cancel-mid-run supported. No backend changes — reuses Phase B save endpoint.

attributes.title: Methodology rule: don't emit entity.progressed on a completed T3
attributes.summary: T3-cache-build appeared live in the cache because the unified-edges fix on 2026-05-27 emitted entity.progressed on it (flipping state from dead back to live per the state machine). That work belonged to T2-storage's architecture, not T3-cache-build. Rule going forward: post-completion work on a T3's theme belongs on its T2 parent; genuine continuation of a closed T3 requires entity.reopened + paired decision; bug-fix follow-on warrants a follow-on T3. Future lint check: any plan with derived_state=live AND a completed event but no reopened event indicates either a missing reopen+decision or scope-creep that should have been ascribed to the T2.

attributes.title: T3-analyser-live-model-catalog — fetch the model list live from /v1/models
attributes.summary: Bug-fix follow-on to T3-analyser-phase-a-ephemeral. The analyser hardcoded a now-retired model list (claude-sonnet-4-20250514 et al.) in three places — settings dropdown, cost-dialog picker, and two default fallbacks — causing not_found_error at call time once those snapshots left the account's catalogue. Replaced all hardcoded IDs with a live ModelCatalog that fetches GET /v1/models with the user's key (cached per key), populating both pickers dynamically once a key is provided in the input. defaultId only honours a saved default if still in the catalogue; Estimator gains family-based priceFor() so new snapshots get sane cost estimates without per-ID hardcoding.

attributes.title: T3-flow-view-filtering — isolate / hide / collapse / lifecycle-filter for the workstreams-flow view
attributes.summary: Authored T3 under T2-projection bundling four flow-view focus operations over one new client-side substrate (state.flowFilters + a computeFlowVisibility pre-pass): D1 lifecycle filter (All/Open/Closed, dead==closed); D2 click/gutter isolation to an entity-or-section's transitive spawn-related set, with unisolate banner + Esc; D3 per-entity and per-section eye-hide (keeps a greyed gutter row, suppresses SVG marks); D4 section collapse to a placeholder node with spawn edges rerouted to it. Bundled rather than split because all four share the same code surface (view/app.js, style.css) and mutable filter state, mirroring T3-flow-view-density. No projection/schema/event-shape changes — view-only.

attributes.title: T3-flow-view-controls — Button contrast, gutter-control affordances, isolated-root cues, and a cascade-exemption fix for the flow view
attributes.summary: View-only T3 under T2-projection bundling four control/legibility fixes from an operator review of the flow view, all over view/style.css + view/app.js: D1 global button-contrast fix (scope .toolbar/.sub-toolbar button defaults with :not([class*='btn-']) so coloured .btn-* pills keep their colours, plus tokenise the button palette to :root CSS variables — generalises the local .isolate-clear patch and kills the white-on-white trap); D2 precise-scope the eye-hide cascade superseder exemption (computeSuperseders→computeSupersededPredecessors map; exclude only the specific superseded predecessor from a node's parent set rather than exempting the node wholesale, so hiding T1 now hides its exclusive child T2-analyser); D3 isolated-root affordance (⊗ de-isolate glyph at the focal row + bold-purple .is-isolated-root title); D4 colour-coded, roomier gutter controls. No projection/schema/event-shape change.

attributes.title: T3-milestone-parent-ontology — Milestones hang off Tier-1 (never T2/T3); reattached supersedes the prior spawn; M6 reparented to M1
attributes.summary: Data/ontology half of the same operator review (the view half is T3-flow-view-controls). D1 codifies the milestone-parent rule (a top-level Mn hangs off a Tier-1 plan or a top-level side-quest head, never a T2/T3; sub-milestones nest Mn.p→Mn via dotted index). D2 reparents M6-analyser from T2-analyser to M1-bootstrap via the first real relationship.reattached event, paired with a decision recording the rule; label/index kept for historical honesty. D3 teaches cache-build.py to honour reattached (pre-scan → suppress the prior spawn edge in both event-sourced and frontmatter passes → insert the new to_parent spawn → keep a reattached provenance row). D4 corrects the methodology docs (T1 §2.4 milestone-parent rule, T2-ontology §3.6 reattached-supersedes-prior-spawn, §3.8 the from_entity_id exception). Touches events.jsonl, scripts/cache-build.py, and docs — no view code.

attributes.title: One button component for the whole view; dial back gutter-control whitespace; inbox swimlanes always last
attributes.summary: Operator-review round 2 (view half). Headline: a DRY, location-independent button system replacing the .toolbar/.sub-toolbar descendant-colour selectors + :not() specificity hacks that keep causing white-on-white regressions (round 1's :not([class*=btn-]) inflated the base to (0,3,1) and beat .toolbar button.active (0,2,1), so the active flow button renders white-on-white). New model: base `button` (0,0,1) neutral pill; single-class state (button.active), disabled (button:disabled), and variant (.btn-*) layers each cleanly outrank the base — no location coupling, no :not(), no !important. Plus two polish tweaks on the same file surface: gutter-control box/gap dialled ~halfway back (gctrls gap 6->4px, gctrl 22->18px square, font 13->12 / swimlane 14->13), and inbox-item swimlanes always sorted to the very last section in both swimlane modes.

attributes.title: Rename the derived lifecycle state dead -> closed everywhere
attributes.summary: Operator-review round 2 (ontology half). Rename the derived derived_state value 'dead' to 'closed' across cache-build.py (state map), projection-emit.py (state_counts + dead_count->closed_count), summary-emit.py (labels/heading), audit-orphans.sql, view/app.js (header stat, states array, lifecycle predicates, badge css classes), view/style.css (--color-dead/.badge.dead/.now-badge.dead), and the T2-ontology derived-state table. Safe with no event migration: 'dead' is never stored in the event log (events record entity.completed/cancelled/superseded; the terminal state is derived), so a cache rebuild re-derives every entity under the new label. Also removes the existing inconsistency where the Open/Closed filter and 'Recently closed' heading already say 'closed' while the header/badges say 'dead'. Operator decision 2026-06-01: 'closed', applied everywhere incl. the internal value.

attributes.title: T3-event-sourced-relationships — make the event log the single source of truth for entity relationships
attributes.summary: Authored T3 under T2-storage to fix the divergent-source-of-truth defect found in M1 close-out: a plan's parentage (t2_parent / milestone) is currently read from four places that can disagree (frozen entity.created cache snapshot, frontmatter-derived graph edge off that snapshot, live planning/*.md frontmatter read in projection-emit compute_milestone_progress, and the dead relationship.reattached path). Design decisions: (D-A) add an `axis` discriminator {t2-parent,milestone} to relationship.reattached, bumping events schema 0.2.0->0.3.0; (D-B) fold edges from the event stream last-write-wins per (entity,axis), entity.created seeds, each reattached rewrites; (D-C) projection-emit reads parentage from the cache, never from live frontmatter; (D-D) frontmatter demoted to a creation-time seed per T1 §3.1; (D-E) correct T2-storage §3.8 and annotate T1 §2.4. The analyser M1->M6 re-tag is deferred into this plan as its first acceptance test. §8 Q1 flags the milestone placement for sign-off. Status draft; do not implement until placement confirmed.

attributes.title: M1.2-relationship-ssot — Make entity relationships a single source of truth
attributes.summary: Focused sub-milestone of M1 (milestone_index 1.2), attached to M1-bootstrap. Created because M1 close-out dogfooding surfaced a single-source-of-truth defect inside the tracker: a plan's parentage (t2_parent / milestone) is read from four places that can disagree (frozen entity.created cache snapshot; the frontmatter-derived spawn edge cache-build synthesises from that snapshot; the live planning/*.md frontmatter re-read in projection-emit compute_milestone_progress; and the dead relationship.reattached path). M1.2 makes parentage a projection of the event log, turns relationship.reattached into a live move primitive with an axis discriminator, and demotes frontmatter to a creation seed. Sole constituent: T3-event-sourced-relationships (its first acceptance test is the analyser re-tag). This is M1 hardening, not new auto-extract capability — hence a decimal M1.x sub-milestone rather than folding into M2. Establishes the Mn.m sub-milestone pattern (M1.1 = analyser, currently mis-filed as M6; renumber deferred). Required a backward-compatible loosening of plan-frontmatter.schema.json (decimal milestone ids + numeric milestone_index).

attributes.title: Automated extraction takes over
attributes.summary: Second milestone authored. Capability unlock: per-commit events extracted automatically instead of hand-rolled. Two shaping decisions from 2026-06-02 brainstorming: (1) SKILL-ONLY — primary trigger is an in-session /apt-extract slash-command, not an autonomous claude -p pre-commit hook (a headless hook spends a separate metered call per commit + blocks git commit ~10-20s; the in-session skill reuses the running session, no extra meter, runs the session's model); the autonomous hook is deferred to a later/M4-adjacent milestone for non-session committers. (2) SHADOW-DEV then FULL CUTOVER — develop the extractor against a configurable shadow dir (APT_DATA_DIR=.agent-plan-tracker-auto) so the 223 hand-rolled canonical events are never corrupted; once trusted, flip config to canonical and auto-extract forward (history preserved, not re-extracted). Not greenfield: lifts + hardens the existing scripts/backfill/ prototype core to schema 0.2.0. Five T3s: extraction-core, configurable-data-dir (T2-storage), apt-extract-skill, extraction-idempotency, cutover-to-auto. Excludes the autonomous hook, M3 cleanliness gate, M4 packaging, M5 backfill, sub-agent recursion (unless a real diff overflows).

Make the data directory configurable via APT_DATA_DIR. Shared path resolver (env var -> default -> .agent-plan-tracker/); repoint cache-build, projection-emit, summary-emit, serve; gitignore .agent-plan-tracker-auto/. Foundation T3, parallel to T3-apt-capture-skill. Permanent product capability (M4 installs need it too).

Codify the event-capture discipline as a skill — instructions the in-session agent follows to emit well-formed schema-0.2.0 events. Contains: ontology summary (25 event types, 5 entity types, fulcrum-decision pairing), entity identification rules, entity.created-first rule, commit.recorded semantics, append-only accumulation model, .last-capture timestamp on completion. M2 headline deliverable. Name TBD: /apt-capture or /apt-save.

Tiny pre-commit hook (shell script, no LLM) that rejects commits when staged files are newer than .last-capture timestamp. Enforces capture-before-commit discipline at zero cost — a timestamp comparison, no network, no block. Includes manual install instructions + convenience install script. Depends on T3-apt-capture-skill (writes .last-capture).

Final M2 T3 — validation + config flip + decision record. Shadow-validate the capture skill over a stretch of real work (operator eyeballs output), flip APT_DATA_DIR to canonical, record the cutover decision event, confirm repack-validate green, clean up the shadow dir. Procedural, not code.

Add the draft→accepted lifecycle for all planning entities. New entity.accepted standard event (draft→live, all 5 entity types, not a fulcrum); new draft derived state — entity.created now lands draft (was live); entity.extended becomes draft-preserving (otherwise unchanged — still reopens closed entities, same as entity.progressed). Schema bump 0.2.0→0.3.0. Foundation T3, prerequisite for T3-apt-capture-skill, whose draft gate forbids entity.progressed against draft entities.

attributes.title: commit.recorded entity-subject drift: ontology prose vs recent practice
attributes.summary: T2-ontology §3.7 specifies commit.recorded carries no entity_type/entity_id, but every recent seal (0.2.0/0.3.0 era) sets them to the commit's primary entity. Needs a ruling: amend §3.7 to bless the primary-entity convention, or strip the fields from future seals. The /apt-capture skill teaches recent practice pending the ruling.

attributes.title: main's log stays a trustworthy record
attributes.summary: Third milestone authored from the 2026-06-09 design conversation. Core reframe (operator ruling): the gate protects the MEDIUM, not the content — the consumer is the next agent doing a cold read of main's log. Visible mess (orphans, stalled entities, unresolved HITL) is the tracker succeeding: true state, merges freely, dashboard tier. Blocking = corruption of the record only: schema violations, dangling references, unsealed trailing runs, implementation-on-draft, resurrection-without-reopen, fulcrum-without-decision. No override machinery — integrity defects are repaired, never overridden. Three shaping decisions: (1) stance-neutral gate-check core + pluggable enforcement adapters (pre-push default, manual; skill-procedural via /apt-merge is primary; CI is a future M4-adjacent thin caller — no GitHub Actions dependency); (2) branch-side reconciliation doctrine, not a merge-arbitration program — in-session agent reconciles on the branch before main moves, main's log is the prefix, contradictions surface to the operator, reconciliation events sealed by the merge commit, rebase acceptable; (3) committed .apt-config.toml at repo root for blocking/warn lists + data_dir (hardcoding rejected as riskier, not YAGNI). Three T3s: integrity-composite (T2-projection), gate-core (T2-extraction), apt-merge-skill (T2-extraction). DoD includes the self-referential acceptance test: this branch lands on main via /apt-merge with gate-check green. Supersedes-in-part T2-extraction §3.7–3.8 and T2-projection §3.5 (correction notes added); resolves T2-extraction §7 Q1 (dissolved by reframe) and Q2 (config file).

Foundation T3: one composite answering 'can a cold reader trust this log?'. Blocking checks: schema validation, referential integrity (decision event_ids, relationship from-entities, lifecycle-without-created), sealed tail, implementation-on-draft (backstop for the skill's advisory draft gate, honours same-block implicit-work carve-out), resurrection-without-reopen (branch-agnostic — also catches cross-branch contradictions post-merge), fulcrum-without-decision (existing audit promoted). Warn tier: frontmatter-vs-event drift (the M1.2 IOU), orphans, stalled, long-blockers (existing audits demoted by the reframe). Config: .apt-config.toml at repo root, tomllib (stdlib ≥ 3.11), gate.blocking/gate.warn lists + storage.data_dir (the never-built middle layer of M2's resolution order). Implementation: scripts/gate-composite.py, stdlib-only, exit 0 clean (warnings printed) / 1 blocking. Supersedes the T3-cleanliness-gate-projection candidate (T2-projection §5).

The boundary check and where it fires. scripts/gate-check.sh entry point (resolve data dir env → .apt-config.toml → default, run gate-composite.py, surface report + exit code) — the single contract every adapter calls. Enforcement topology: skill-procedural primary (/apt-merge — only path that sees local merges), pre-push adapter belt-and-braces (refuses pushes updating refs/heads/main when gate-check fails), manual/future-CI thin callers (M4-adjacent). Installer extends the M2 install-hook.sh pattern with --at=pre-push|manual, same idempotency contract as capture-guard (fresh / identical-noop / differs-refuse, symlink-aware). Supersedes the T3-pre-merge-hook and T3-server-side-cleanliness-gate candidates (T2-extraction §4).

Branch-side reconciliation doctrine as skills/apt-merge/SKILL.md — doctrine + agent + skill, not an arbitration program. Procedure: pick the lightest sufficient integration (ff / rebase preferred — seals match message_first_line so the log is rebase-tolerant by design / merge only when both logs grew); the events.jsonl conflict is the designed trigger, never suppressed (no union merge driver); recipe: main's log is the prefix, branch blocks append after, never reorder or edit within blocks; semantic pass surfaces same-entity contradictions to the operator, their ruling becomes reconciliation events in a fresh block sealed by the merge commit (capture guard firing on conflicted merges is correct; clean merges rightly bypass hooks); run gate-check before landing; degrades to a documented manual procedure for non-agentic users. Verification 1 is the self-referential acceptance test (this branch transits its own doctrine, operator-triggered). Supersedes the T3-merge-conflict-handler candidate (T2-extraction §4).

attributes.title: the plugin attaches to any project
attributes.summary: Fourth milestone, authored from the post-M3 design conversation ('how does a downstream agent know how to install and use this?'). Design stance: knowledge is delivered just-in-time through three channels — skill descriptions (when to act, already built), enforcement refusals (when discipline slips, already built), and bootstrap + session orientation (once per repo / once per session — M4's build). Shaping decisions: (1) code/data split is absolute — an attached repo carries log + config + hook copies, never toolchain; the toolchain home is the plugin install (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT), installers bake paths at init; (2) init is a user-triggered idempotent command, no postinstall magic (resolves T2-packaging §7 Q2 as leaned); (3) the APV rename executes in T3-toolchain-portability (operator ruling 2026-06-10); (4) existing projects attach from now — history mining stays M5. Install wave: T3-toolchain-portability, T3-project-init-flow, T3-session-orientation, T3-distribution. Later wave: T3-autonomous-extractor (claude -p, placement is §7 Q1 operator call). DoD centres on a cold-agent pass: a non-dogfood sandbox repo runs capture->guard->gate->merge end-to-end on plugin-delivered knowledge alone.

attributes.title: every reference resolves via the toolchain home
attributes.summary: Foundation T3: one resolution chain (env -> repo-vendored -> CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT -> PATH) applied to skills, hooks, installers, scripts; installers bake the resolved toolchain path into hook copies. The APV rename (agent-plan-tracker -> agent-plan-visualiser, APT_* -> APV_*, apt-* skills -> apv-*, .apt-config.toml -> .apv-config.toml) executes here, live surfaces only — the event log, closed plans and git history are never rewritten; the dogfood data dir stays .agent-plan-tracker pinned via [storage] data_dir. Verification: all suites green post-rename; a portability sandbox with toolchain only at a simulated plugin root; grep audit of live surfaces.

attributes.title: one command attaches a repo
attributes.summary: The init command (final name post-rename): preconditions, seed data dir + empty events.jsonl (the one sanctioned creation site) + .apv-config.toml, install the three git hooks via the existing installers (their fresh/identical/differs contract is the idempotency story), offer a CLAUDE.md block (never write unasked), print next steps; re-run = audit-and-repair mode. Existing repos attach from now (backfill is M5). Consolidates T2-packaging §5's cli-install-command + target-project-init-flow candidates.

attributes.title: the session knows, without being told
attributes.summary: The third knowledge channel: hooks/hooks.json SessionStart entry detects the repo fingerprint and injects one orientation line (silent in untracked repos — no adoption nagging); the formal skills/using-agent-plan-visualiser skill carries the spec floor and T2-packaging §3.4's instruction shape (prefer scripts/, save reusable queries to scripts/local/, cheatsheet surface, philosophies for judgement); cheatsheet first content pass.

attributes.title: the artefact that delivers the plugin
attributes.summary: Decide the distribution mechanism (marketplace vs npm vs both — decision event), build the artefact, verify Cowork compatibility, ship the CI gate-adapter template M3 deferred (thin gate-check --ref caller as template, no Actions dependency), README quickstart. Clean-environment install simulation carries M4 §6's cold-agent pass. Consolidates T2-packaging §5's npm-package-config + cowork-compat-verify candidates.

attributes.title: capture for commits no session agent saw
attributes.summary: Authored post-ceremony under the M4 §7 Q1 ruling (in-wave, sooner rather than later — claude -p runs within subscription allowances, dissolving the cost concern behind T2-extraction §3.4's deferral). The same capture contract, produced autonomously at commit time: stamp-fresh passthrough (session capture stays primary), input bundle -> claude -p -> schema + write-rule validation (the extractor may never emit entity.accepted), clean appends seal-and-stamp, ambiguity defaults to halt with a needs-review file (T2-extraction §3.6). Opt-in via the init command; sub-agent recursion and backfill reuse stay out of the first cut. Supersedes the T3-autonomous-extraction-hook candidate name. Open questions: commit-msg vs pre-commit hook (lean commit-msg — the seal needs the message), model/prompt budget (empirical), confidence 'derived' for autonomous events (lean yes).

Surfaced during T3-toolchain-portability: view/app.js (and the serve flow) read ../../.agent-plan-tracker/{projection.json,events.jsonl,inbox/} literally — correct for the dogfood repo, wrong for .apv adopters. A portable view needs serve.py to inject the resolved data dir (or a config-aware loader). Untriaged; likely rides T3-session-orientation or its own T3 under T2-analyser/T2-projection.

Fifth milestone: history becomes record. Mines existing project history into the log honestly — bitemporal anchoring, origin provenance, three-tier Why (the 2026-07-03 ruling is the ground). Three waves: the contract pair (0.4.0 schema + historical-projection UI, co-designed), the machinery (backfill workflow, why-triage pass, mapping template), the proof (self-referential backfill of this repo's pre-adoption history).

Wave-1 contract T3, paired with T3-historical-projection-ui: schemas/0.4.0 (origin field, backfill_run, commit_ref on backfilled seals), event-time state derivation in cache-build, origin-aware gate discipline, projection carries the UI contract. Existing log validates unmigrated.

Wave-1 contract T3, paired with T3-origin-provenance-schema: event-time unfurling in the flow view, ghosted provenance rendering + toggle, open-question rendering for backfill hypotheses, and the data-dir hardcode fix (absorbs the 2026-06-10.view-hardcodes-dogfood-data-dir inbox item).

Wave 2: formalise the M5-lite scripts/backfill orchestrator against the ratified doctrine — 0.4.0 emission with origin + run id + commit_ref seals, append-to-live in guard-transiting chunks, resumable, hypothesis side-channel, mapping-note brief, toolchain-home portable.

Wave 2: the post-walk batch triage — one operator sitting converts walk hypotheses to recollected decisions (operator as actor) or open hitl-questions with candidates; idempotent; appended in an ordinary captured triage commit.

Wave 2, parallel: the canonical retrospective-mapping template (YAML structured parts + markdown narrative, known-pivots entries shaped as triage input) + one worked example + extractor-brief wiring + absent-note pre-flight warning.

Surfaced at the M5 ceremony: acceptance ceremonies are enforced only lazily — the draft gate blocks implementation-on-draft at capture and at the gate, but nothing PROMPTS a pending ceremony, so an authored-but-unaccepted plan (T3-autonomous-extractor, 23 days) can silently sit while everyone believes it built. Candidates: a warn-level audit (drafts older than N days, or drafts whose milestone is in build), a session-orientation mention of pending drafts, or a ceremony checklist in the milestone-close flow.

decisions.text: Architecture pivot: browser-direct to Anthropic API + thin server wrapper, instead of the inbox item's proposed claude-CLI-via-server. Browser-direct keeps API credentials with the user's account (no server-side key store), makes the cost model transparent, and makes summaries durable across sessions via localStorage. The server wrapper shrinks to three endpoints (clean-check, save-summary, invalidate-summary) — git state + filesystem only, no LLM credentials. Additional scope captured in T2-analyser that the inbox item didn't have: summaries as first-class events (analysis.live-summary, analysis.invalidated), per-summary markdown files, clean-tree guard for sequencing within commits, cascade invalidation, bulk mode with Anthropic prompt caching, flow-view rendering of saved summaries. Superseding the inbox item rather than amending it because the design delta is substantial — the inbox proposal could not have evolved into this without rewriting; preserving the original as a fulcrum'd dead node is honest history.

Milestone-parent rule: a top-level milestone Mn hangs off a Tier-1 plan (the project's intent) or off a top-level side-quest's Tier-1-equivalent (e.g. P1) — never off a T2 or T3. A milestone is a when-axis node; its parent is the intent it sequences toward, not a theme. Sub-milestones nest on the milestone axis: Mn.p hangs off Mn, Mn.p.q off Mn.p (dotted index = a finer-grained delivery slice). The dotted scheme is forward-looking notation; existing flat indices (M1..M6) are grandfathered. Corollary on the relationship.reattached primitive: it does not merely annotate a move — in derived projections it supersedes the prior spawns edge (the from_parent spawns child edge is suppressed and a to_parent spawns child edge replaces it), so the node actually moves in the spawn graph the view and tree read; cache-build applies this rewrite. Applied here to reparent M6-analyser from T2-analyser to M1-bootstrap (event d8000003) while keeping its label and index for historical honesty.

Lifecycle-vocabulary decision (operator, 2026-06-01): the derived terminal lifecycle state is renamed from 'dead' to 'closed', applied EVERYWHERE including the internal derived_state value — not just user-facing labels — so code and UI share one vocabulary. Rationale: 'dead' is harsh for an operator-facing tool and was already inconsistent with the Open/Closed filter and the 'Recently closed' summary heading. Safe because 'dead' is a derived label never written to the event log (transitions are entity.completed/cancelled/superseded); a cache rebuild re-derives all entities under 'closed' with no event migration. The four derived states become live/dormant/closed/orphaned (+unknown). Companion approach decision: flow-view buttons move to a DRY, location-independent component system (base `button` element rule + single-class state/variant/disabled layers that each outrank the base) to permanently end the white-on-white regressions caused by location-based descendant selectors patched with :not() specificity hacks.

The event log is the single source of truth for entity relationships (thematic t2_parent and milestone membership). Frontmatter t2_parent/milestone is demoted to a creation-time declaration that seeds the first edge via entity.created; every subsequent move is a relationship.reattached event carrying an `axis` discriminator (t2-parent | milestone) that rewrites the edge in the cache and renders the reshuffle in the graph. This resolves T1 §5 Q9 and overrides the §2.4 'would create noise' worry (milestone moves are infrequent and worth recording). Chosen over frontmatter-as-SSOT (which broke during the M1 analyser re-tag: cache, graph, and live-read projection disagreed about the same fact) because it restores §3.1/§3.2 (git/event-log primary; state is a projection, no parallel divergent stores). Frontmatter-vs-event drift becomes possible and is caught by an M3 audit rather than asserted structurally impossible. Implemented by T3-event-sourced-relationships (requires events schema bump 0.2.0->0.3.0 for the axis attribute).

M2 extraction is delivered as an in-session /apt-extract slash-command, NOT an autonomous claude -p pre-commit hook. Rationale (operator, 2026-06-02): a headless per-commit hook spends a separate metered API call on every commit and blocks git commit ~10-20s, whereas the in-session skill reuses the session already running (no separate meter, no block) and runs the session's model — often Opus, which is both cheaper-at-the-margin and higher-quality than a Sonnet headless call. This overrides T2-extraction's original hook-as-primary design (§3.4). The autonomous hook is deferred (not cancelled) to a later/M4-adjacent milestone for committers OUTSIDE a Claude Code session (humans committing directly, CI, teammates); it reuses the same extractor core, so only the invocation differs. Companion decision: develop the extractor against a configurable shadow data dir (APT_DATA_DIR) so the canonical hand-rolled history is protected during tuning, then full-cutover by flipping config — existing events preserved, not re-extracted.

M2 rewrite correction (operator + agent, 2026-06-08). The 2026-06-02 M2 draft over-engineered the design by treating the skill as a program: it proposed lifting backfill.py's functions into a shared 'extraction core module' with input/output contracts, a 'pending mode' with delta detection, a 'catch-up mode' over historical commits, and idempotency guards. Three corrections: (1) A Claude Code skill is just instructions the in-session agent follows — the agent has full context, knows what it did, and appends events directly. No separate program needed. (2) Retroactive extraction over old commits is M5 (backfill), not M2. M2 captures events for current work before it's committed. (3) The commit-discipline hook is a tiny timestamp guard (.last-capture), not an LLM call. The skill writes the timestamp last after appending events; the hook rejects commits when staged files postdate it. This cuts M2 from 5 T3s to 4, drops the extraction-core/idempotency/catch-up T3s entirely, and leaves backfill.py untouched for M5.

Renumber the analyser milestone M6-analyser -> M1.1-analyser (fulcrum entity.renamed). This REVERSES the M1.2-era operator decision (events bdd4d341 / 157a78cf) that dropped the renumber and grandfathered the M6 label + reparented to M1-bootstrap. Rationale for reversing: the analyser is genuinely the first M1 sub-milestone and the flat M6 label has been a standing 'historical whoopsie'; the only reasons to grandfather were (a) entity.renamed was inert/unbuilt and (b) it would churn the load-bearing filename + ~24 events. (a) is now resolved by building the identity-migration fold; (b) is accepted as a one-off correctness cost (the canonical events.jsonl is append-only — old lines are untouched; only 3 new events are appended). Ontology consequence (T2-ontology §3.11 amended): entity.renamed MAY change an entity's canonical id — it is an identity migration that cache-build folds last-write-wins across the entity's own events, relationship endpoints, and frontmatter seeds; the prior rule 'the canonical id does not change across rename' is superseded. §3.10 consequence: entity.renamed is state-neutral (removed from STATE_FROM_EVENT) so renaming a closed entity does not resurrect it. Children follow the rename for free (no per-child events); the file moves M6-analyser.md -> M1.1-analyser.md and milestone_index 6 -> 1.1.

Resolve the progressed-after-completed state-flip question: entity.progressed on a completed entity flips it back to live per the state machine — this is correct behaviour, not a bug. The entity then requires explicit re-closure (entity.completed). The methodology rules documented in the inbox item are sound: (1) completed T3s are closed history; (2) post-completion theme-work targets the T2 parent; (3) genuine continuation requires entity.reopened + paired decision; (4) bug-fix follow-on spawns a new T3. The lint query (live + completed + no reopened) remains useful for M3 cleanliness gate.

Bootstrap exception for the draft gate: T3-entity-accepted is itself a draft entity being progressed, which the very rule it introduces (no entity.progressed against draft entities) would forbid. The rule cannot bind before it exists, so this one T3 is implemented under pre-0.3.0 rules. All subsequent M2 T3s must be entity.accepted before implementation work begins.

First acceptance ceremony after the 0.3.0 flip (18 entities derived draft under the new state machine). Operator accepted the active spine (T1-top-level, M2-auto-extract, T2-extraction) and all four remaining M2 T3s — clearing them for implementation work under the draft gate. Deliberately left draft: T2-ingest (M5 territory, not yet shaped for execution) and all 10 inbox items from 2026-05-23 (untriaged captures — draft is exactly their semantic; each gets accepted individually at triage).

Anonymous seals. A commit may affect many entities; there is no basis to arbitrarily privilege one as the seal's reference entity at write time. commit.recorded therefore carries no entity_type/entity_id — commit-to-plan grouping is projection-time work over the positional rollup. The 16 entity-tagged seals from the 0.2.0-0.3.0 era are write-time drift: preserved append-only, ruled invalid as a pattern, not to be imitated. Ontology section 3.7 prose stands as written; SKILL.md sections 2/5/8 rewritten to match.

Cutover to skill-driven capture, executed via the organic-evidence variant: the designed shadow phase was rendered redundant because the skill's first two uses (3acb6b0 self-referential, b9dd4b7 fresh-context agent) were already canonical and repack-green. Operator reviewed and blessed those captures as the validation evidence. /apt-capture is now the canonical producer; the hand-rolled event history is preserved append-only beneath it; the capture-guard hook was installed live before this close-out so the sealing commit itself transits the guard. git commit --no-verify remains the sanctioned escape hatch for trivial plan-less commits.

Four operator rulings shape M3 (design conversation, 2026-06-09). (1) The gate protects the medium, not the content: its consumer is the next agent's cold read of main's log. Visible mess — orphans, stalled entities, unresolved HITL questions — is the tracker succeeding and merges freely; blocking is reserved for corruption of the record; there is no override machinery (integrity defects are repaired, never overridden); staleness is not a smell (a draft sitting until someone acts on it is doing its job — the real draft smell is implementation events against draft entities). (2) Enforcement is a stance-neutral core with pluggable adapters: git hooks as sane default now, architected so future work can add CI/PR enforcement — no GitHub Actions dependency; the /apt-merge skill is the primary, procedural enforcement path. (3) Merge doctrine, not merge program: the in-session agent reconciles branch-side before main moves; rebase is acceptable; merge only when there is actually something to merge. (4) Strictness config lives in a committed .apt-config.toml at repo root — hardcoding rejected as the riskier option, not as YAGNI ('it's not yagni at all').

Epoch rule for replay-semantics checks (settled during the T3-integrity-composite build, 2026-06-10). The 0.3.0 capture discipline (created-first, draft gate, explicit reopen) is enforced only from the schema regime that introduced it; pre-0.3.0 events are judged by their own regime. Keying differs by check: implementation-on-draft keys on the ENTITY's birth regime (its entity.created schema_version) — draft is a creation-time property, and cache-build's retroactive created→draft backfill is a replay convenience, not a historical claim; the record itself validates this (the first acceptance ceremony accepted exactly the 7 plans born into 0.3.0, while T3-entity-accepted, born 0.2.0, needed none — resolving the line-255 chicken-and-egg without fudging). Lifecycle-without-created and resurrection-without-reopen key on the OFFENDING event's schema_version. Structural checks (per-version schema routing, dangling decision refs, relationship existence, sealed-tail, fulcrum-without-decision) apply to all epochs — never legitimate in any regime. EPOCH = (0,3,0) is hardcoded in gate-composite.py as an ontology fact, deliberately exempt from the config-over-hardcode ruling that produced .apt-config.toml: which checks block is a project preference; when the discipline began is not.

Build rulings for T3-gate-core: (1) the seal-commit correspondence check lives in gate-check, the composite stays log-only — T3-integrity-composite §6 Q1 confirmed as built; direction is log->git only (unsealed commits are sanctioned --no-verify trivia) and matching is by message, not SHA (rebase-tolerant; catches squash/reword orphaning the record). (2) The epoch doctrine extends to the seal discipline, keyed on the seal's own schema_version: exact-match is 0.3.0 capture-skill law; the 7 pre-0.3.0 loose seals whose commits exist under slightly different subjects NOTICE, never block. (3) Mid-flow tolerance in filesystem mode — seals beyond HEAD's committed extent name the commit to come (capture-before-commit), NOTICE never BLOCK; --ref mode is strict. (4) The pre-push adapter gates only refs/heads/main and skips deletions — T3-gate-core §6 Q1 resolved. (5) Schemas resolve against the toolchain home, never --repo-root: a gated repo carries a log, not a copy of the schemas.

Build rulings for T3-apt-merge-skill: (1) §6 Q1 — a clean merge commit needs no seal: git bypasses pre-commit on automatic merge commits, nothing happened to the log, and sealless merge commits are tolerated by design (positional rollup skips them; the seal-commit check runs log->git only). A conflicted merge is the designed opposite: the guard firing is correct, the minimum capture is a seal-only block, contradictions add reconciliation events before the seal. (2) §6 Q2 and M3-clean-gate §8 Q3 — the two-branch contradiction sandbox is required, not stretch: the real merge of this branch is a pure fast-forward (main sits at the merge-base) and exercises no conflict. (3) check_resurrection recognises the healed shape — a later entity.reopened resolves the violations before it: every blocking check must be append-only-repairable, since the recipe linearises a cross-branch contradiction as closed-then-progressed and nothing can be inserted before the violation; what blocks at the boundary is the unresolved contradiction, and the fulcrum check guarantees the ruling's paired decision. (4) gate-check runs after the merge commit, from the branch — both parents reachable so every seal resolves; the invariant is 'before main moves', not 'before the merge commit exists'. (5) aptlib parses a present config on pythons without tomllib via a strict minimal TOML subset reader, failing loud on anything outside it — a present config silently ignored is the exact risk hardcoding was rejected for (M3-clean-gate §3.3).

Operator ruling (al, 2026-06-10): the gate must fire on LOCAL merges, not just pushes — the pre-push adapter alone cannot see a local merge, and the skill-procedural path is discipline, not mechanism. Implementation rulings: (1) the adapter is a reference-transaction hook, not pre-merge-commit — a fast-forward merge (the standard /apt-merge landing) runs no merge or commit hook whatsoever; reference-transaction is the only hook class that observes every move of refs/heads/main, so the M3 invariant is enforced literally: main never points at a red log. (2) It gates strictly (--ref on the prepared oid, the same contract as pre-push) and covers merge commits, direct commits on main, amends and resets alike; branch refs, deletions and no-op updates pass untouched. (3) reference-transaction has no --no-verify, so the sanctioned escape hatch is explicit and loud: APT_SKIP_GATE=1, for tooling breakage, never for landing red logs — integrity defects are repaired, not overridden. (4) Verified empirically that git updates the worktree before the ref transaction in an ff merge: repo-relative gate-check resolution therefore works even when the merge being gated is the one delivering the toolchain.

Operator ruling (al, 2026-06-10): the project renames to agent-plan-visualiser (APV). Assessment that shaped the execution plan: this is not a one-shot find-and-replace — the event log is append-only law (hundreds of historical path/name references in summaries, command strings and seals stay as true record), closed plans are archaeology, and git history is immutable; the live breaking surface (data dir name, config filename, aptlib module, APT_* env vars, apt-* skill names, installed hook copies, plugin dir + manifest) is exactly the surface T3-toolchain-portability re-plumbs through the toolchain home anyway. Therefore: rename rides that T3 at near-zero marginal cost rather than being done now and touched twice. The dogfood repo's data dir is grandfathered as .agent-plan-tracker via [storage] data_dir — the config middle layer absorbs the brand change with no log surgery. Resolves T2-packaging §7 Q1 (apt was already rejected for the Debian collision; apv clears it).

Operator ruling (al, 2026-06-10): for now, just bundle the plugin. Deployment target is the operator's exfu.ai site (placement and upload flow to be shown later) as a private test channel — test clients install from there and give feedback. The public-distribution question (npm vs Claude Code plugin marketplace vs both) is deferred deliberately, not decided; it reopens when test feedback warrants. Precedent: the exfu-solo plugin already distributes as a bundle via exfu.ai, so the channel pattern exists. Resolves M4-fresh-install §7 Q2 for the test phase and narrows T3-distribution §2.1 from an evaluation task to a build task.

M4 acceptance ceremony rulings (operator al, 2026-06-10): (1) Extractor placement — in-wave, sooner rather than later; the operator's discovery that claude -p runs within subscription allowances dissolves the cost concern that had deferred T2-extraction §3.4's autonomous hook, so T3-autonomous-extractor is authored immediately, depending only on T3-toolchain-portability. (2) Fresh-install data dir is .apv/ — short over brand-consistent; the dogfood repo stays grandfathered on .agent-plan-tracker via config. (3) The init command's CLAUDE.md block is offer-only: init is the only trigger for the offer, no other code path writes or re-offers, and writing requires explicit user acceptance. (4) All remaining leans across the five plans ratified as drafted — acceptance of all five recorded; the extractor T3 is born draft and awaits its own acceptance.

Build rulings for T3-toolchain-portability: (1) Baking is conditional on install-gate.sh --home= — an unconditional bake would weld the shared dogfood hooks (one copy serving the main checkout and every worktree) to a single worktree's path; plugin installs pass CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, vendored installs ship verbatim and the chain (env -> baked home -> repo-relative -> PATH) decides at run time; installer idempotency compares the RENDERED copy. (2) apvlib's default data dir moves to .apv per the M4 §7 Q3 ruling; the dogfood repo pins .agent-plan-tracker via [storage] data_dir, making the rename a non-event for the record; capture-guard mirrors the same resolution in dependency-free POSIX (one-key sed). (3) gate-check's repo-root defaults to git rev-parse --show-toplevel — the toolchain home no longer implies the gated repo. (4) Schemas stay byte-frozen across the rename: they are epoch contract artefacts validating historical events, and 0.3.0 structurally patterns the data dir's real (kept) name. (5) The legacy sandboxes' fixture repos adopt .apv — fixture data dirs are test scaffolding, not the dogfood record.

Operator ruling 2026-07-03 on backfill representation (design conversation post-M4 install wave): (1) the log becomes officially bitemporal — backfilled events append at the record tail and anchor to historical event time via per-historical-commit seals carrying commit_ref; projections order by event time; the append-only law is never bent and no synthetic history is created. (2) Provenance is a first-class origin field, not a confidence overload — backfilled events are permanently distinguishable from contemporaneous capture, gate discipline is origin-aware, and the UI renders provenance. (3) Historical Why is never fabricated: recovered rationale cites its source, recollected rationale requires the operator's confirmation at a batch triage pass, and unconfirmable rationale is recorded as open hitl-questions carrying candidate hypotheses — a plausible lie is worse than an honest gap, because agents act on decisions. Schema 0.4.0 and enforcement land with M5; the historical-projection UI is co-designed with the schema before M5 T3s build.

M5 acceptance ceremony rulings (operator, 2026-07-03): (Q1) the self-referential backfill proof runs against a disposable copy of this repo first — the real dogfood log is appended only by a separate explicit operator trigger after the rehearsal is green; (Q2) exfu_website (plugin/ subdir) is the canonical first non-native reference target; (Q3) T3-autonomous-extractor is accepted and built immediately — the operator believed it already existed, and the gap between authored and accepted was invisible, which itself is recorded as an inbox item; (Q4) schema 0.4.0 lands at wave 1 so gate and UI work test against it.

Operator rulings at wave-3 staging (2026-07-03): (1) exfu_website is the testable reference AND the rehearsal target — the planned self-referential native test dissolved on discovery that the dogfood repo has zero pre-adoption commits; (2) bulk extraction uses latest Sonnet, never Fable — 'way too expensive' for mechanical per-commit work. Rehearsal staged as a disposable clone with an agent-drafted mapping note pending operator review; the live run is theirs to trigger (nested claude -p cannot authenticate from this session).
